note: Short-range, checkable forecasts. Each has a probability, a deadline and a resolution rule. Resolved forecasts are scored with the Brier score (lower is better; always guessing 50% scores 0.25). A badly posed forecast (one that can't resolve as asked, or asks about something that doesn't exist) may be withdrawn unscored; it stays listed with the reason and the date.

forecasts.question: Google releases Gemini 4 (any tier, public or paid preview) by Nov 30, 2026
forecasts.resolution: An official Google announcement of availability to outside users.
forecasts.context: Resolved Yes: on Oct 13, 2026 Google said Gemini 4 Argon "is now globally available today for developers and enterprises via the API in AI Studio and Gemini platform", and to Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers in the Gemini app; its Gemini API changelog lists Gemini 4 Argon as generally available (GA) under Oct 13 (Google; verified fact). That meets the rule and our Oct 9 clarification, which named paid API customers and Google AI Ultra subscribers.
forecasts.original_context: Kavukcuoglu said Sept 23–24 that Google wants it out "as soon as possible".

corrections.text: Clarification of the resolution rule (the rule itself is unchanged): Google announced Gemini 4 Argon on Sept 30 and is rolling it out first "to a set of trusted cyber defenders through our Fairwind Program". As our Oct 2 wrap-up said, we count that limited access as neither a public nor a paid preview, so it doesn't resolve this forecast; availability to paid API customers or Google AI Ultra subscribers, which Google says comes next, would. Google's Gemini API changelog through Oct 8 lists no Gemini 4 model.

forecasts.question: OpenAI says it has resumed training its frontier models by Oct 31, 2026
forecasts.resolution: An OpenAI statement or credible report that the Sept 27 training pause has ended.
forecasts.context: Resolved Yes: on Oct 23 OpenAI said that "we resumed reinforcement learning (RL) training and internal inference of our frontier models on October 1", after a red-teaming campaign on its training environment (OpenAI; verified fact). Restarting frontier training counts under the rule and our Sept 30 clarification. It was the first OpenAI statement we found that training covered by the pause had resumed. OpenAI's DNS incident report, last updated Sept 25, still said on Oct 23 that "All training, evaluation, and inference with tool-use (defined broadly) of our most capable models remain paused" (OpenAI; verified fact).
forecasts.original_context: This is the second pause in three months, and the safeguards needed to resume are unspecified.

corrections.text: The second pause began Friday Sept 25 (Fortune, NBC), not Sept 27. OpenAI stated its conditions: validate that the DNS sandbox gap is fixed and do more red-teaming, then restart training from scratch. All inference on its most capable models is stopped.

Clarification of the resolution rule (the rule itself is unchanged): OpenAI says it will restart training from scratch once the DNS sandbox fix is validated. A fresh, from-scratch training run of a frontier model counts as resuming training, as does restarting the paused runs. Restarting inference alone, or training only small or non-frontier models, doesn't count.

Our Sept 30 correction dated the start of the pause to Sept 25 (Fortune, NBC). OpenAI's Oct 23 post says it resumed on Oct 1, "11 days after our pause began", which by OpenAI's count puts the start on Sept 20, the day of the DNS incident (our inference). Sept 25 is the "Report updated" date on OpenAI's DNS incident report, which announced the pause. The question, probability and resolution rule are unchanged.

forecasts.question: Anthropic shares begin trading on Nasdaq by Oct 31, 2026
forecasts.resolution: The first day of public trading.
forecasts.context: Resolved No: Anthropic's shares could not begin trading by Oct 31. Anthropic filed its S-1 publicly only on Oct 26, and at about 13:40 PT Oct 30, after the last regular US exchange session before the deadline had closed (Oct 31 is a Saturday), its EDGAR record showed no amended S-1, notice of effectiveness, final prospectus or exchange registration (Form 8-A) (SEC EDGAR; verified fact (part our inference): that no listing could open is our reading of the missing filings). A company that submitted drafts confidentially must file publicly "at least 15 days prior to any road show or, in the absence of a road show, at least 15 days prior to the requested effective date" (SEC; verified fact), so neither Anthropic's roadshow nor, without one, its effectiveness could come before Nov 10 (our arithmetic). Bloomberg reported that marketing could start in the week of Nov 9 at the earliest, with a debut targeted before Thanksgiving (Bloomberg, via XTB; credible report).
forecasts.original_context: The prospectus went public Sept 28, targeting mid-October.
forecasts.marketSource: Polymarket "Will Anthropic IPO by October 31, 2026?", last trade via the public API at 13:15 PT (no bid at the read, so no midpoint; ask 0.1; about $1.53M traded)

corrections.text: The Sept 28 prospectus was a leaked draft seen by Reuters and the FT, not a public filing; Anthropic's S-1 is still confidential (submitted June 1). The 75% rested on that error; it stands as made and will be scored.

forecasts.question: METR publishes a time-horizon estimate for GPT-6 Astra by Nov 30, 2026
forecasts.resolution: A GPT-6 Astra entry on METR's time-horizons page or blog.
forecasts.context: METR's page has shown nothing newer than May 8, and its suite is saturated above 16 hours.

corrections.text: Our context said METR's time-horizons page had shown nothing newer than May 8. It missed a note METR added on Sept 8: "Clarified that this page is no longer actively updated." A GPT-6 Astra estimate is therefore likelier to come, if at all, as a METR blog post, which this forecast also counts (our inference). We found no GPT-6 Astra time-horizon estimate in METR's feed through its Oct 22 post. The question, probability and resolution rule are unchanged.

forecasts.resolution: A public design document or report released by the state.
forecasts.context: Newsom's Sept 18 executive order set the deadline.

corrections.text: EO N-9-26 §3 orders state agencies to send the Governor recommendations by Nov 16, including on requiring a frontier-model kill switch. It does not order a design and does not require publication.

forecasts.voidReason: It asked for a kill-switch "design" that EO N-9-26 never orders: §3 asks for recommendations to the Governor's office by Nov 16 and doesn't require publishing them. forecasts.question: The Clay Institute accepts OpenAI's Navier–Stokes result as solving the Millennium Prize problem by Dec 31, 2026
forecasts.resolution: A Clay Mathematics Institute announcement.
forecasts.context: Clay review is pending, and Clay rules normally require publication plus two years.

corrections.text: Clay review is not pending. Clay takes no submissions and considers a result only after journal publication plus two years, and OpenAI says it won't claim the prize.

forecasts.voidReason: It couldn't resolve Yes by its deadline: Clay considers a result only two years after journal publication, and OpenAI says it won't claim the prize. Replaced by a forecast on journal acceptance by Sep 30, 2027 (navier-journal-by-sep30-2027)

forecasts.question: A peer-reviewed journal accepts OpenAI's Navier–Stokes paper for publication by Sep 30, 2027
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by Sep 30, 2027, a peer-reviewed mathematics or science journal accepts or publishes the paper (or a version with the same main result), shown by the journal's site, an "accepted" note on arXiv or the authors' pages, or a credible report. Preprints, Lean formalisations and conference talks don't count.
forecasts.context: Replaces the withdrawn Clay forecast. The proof checks in Lean and its correctness is uncontested; credit and how autonomously it was found are disputed. Refereeing a result of this size usually takes one to three years, and we don't know whether OpenAI has submitted it to a journal. Journal publication is the first step Clay's rules need.

forecasts.question: California publishes the recommendations due under EO N-9-26 by Nov 30, 2026
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by Nov 30, 2026, the Governor's office, the Government Operations Agency or Cal OES publicly releases the §3 recommendations: the document itself, or a summary that states the recommendation on each of items a–d (onsite verifiers, verified safety filings, a kill switch, loss-of-control incident reporting). A statement that recommendations were delivered, without their content, doesn't count.
forecasts.context: Replaces the withdrawn kill-switch forecast. The signed order (Sept 18) tells the Government Operations Agency, with Cal OES, to submit recommendations to the Governor's office no later than Nov 16, 2026. It doesn't require publishing them, so release depends on the Governor's office; deadlines like this often slip.

forecasts.question: OpenAI releases its post-Astra model, or an external evaluation of it is publicly announced, by Nov 7, 2026
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by the end of Nov 7, 2026 (Pacific), either (a) OpenAI announces that the frontier model it acknowledged on Sept 8, 2026 (the unreleased internal model it said is more capable than GPT-6 Astra) is available to outside users, or (b) an outside evaluator (such as METR, UK AISI, US CAISI, Apollo Research or Epoch AI), or OpenAI, publicly announces that an outside evaluator has evaluated that model. OpenAI's own internal evaluations, and access or testing that nobody announces, don't count. If GPT-6.1 Astra (whose release OpenAI cancelled on Sept 28) proves to be the same model, its release or announced external evaluation counts. No otherwise. This tracks our alarm trigger W2 (criteria v1.1), which this model meets on Nov 7 unless it is released or an external evaluation of it is announced.
forecasts.context: Resolved No: by the end of Nov 7, 2026 (Pacific), OpenAI had not made the post-Astra model it acknowledged on Sept 8 available to outside users, and no outside evaluation of it had been announced. Read on Nov 13, OpenAI's Deployment Safety Hub lists the Nov 5 GPT-6 Cyber System Card as its newest entry, OpenAI's news feed has no item between 08:00 GMT Nov 6 and 08:00 GMT Nov 9 and none since that announces the model, METR's newest blog post is dated Nov 5 and UK AISI's newest blog post Oct 26 (OpenAI; METR; UK AISI; verified fact (part our inference): that none covers the post-Astra model is our reading). Our daily checks of NIST CAISSI, Apollo Research and Irregular through Nov 9 found no outside evaluation of it either (our inference, from our daily checks). GPT-6 Cyber, released Nov 5 with outside assessments, is 'a cyber-specialized variant of GPT-6 Astra' (OpenAI; verified fact), not the post-Astra model (our inference). Alarm condition W2, which this forecast tracked, was met on Nov 7, day 60, and the model was still unreleased on Nov 13, day 66 (our inference, from our daily checks).
forecasts.original_context: On Sept 8 OpenAI credited its Navier–Stokes result to an unreleased internal model that it says is significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra. Since Sept 25 it has paused all training, evaluation and tool-using inference of its most capable models, and on Sept 28 it said it won't release GPT-6.1 Astra. As of our Oct 2 check, none of METR, UK AISI, Epoch, CAISI or Apollo Research lists an evaluation of the post-Astra model. Politico reported on Sept 24 (via The Next Web), citing a senior administration official, that the White House asked OpenAI and Anthropic not to share new models with UK AISI until the US government has tested them. We think a release before Nov 7 is unlikely during the pause, and US government pre-release testing is usually not made public.

corrections.text: Our context said that since Sept 25 OpenAI had paused all training, evaluation and tool-using inference of its most capable models. OpenAI said on Oct 23 that it "resumed reinforcement learning (RL) training and internal inference of our frontier models on October 1", the day before this forecast was made (OpenAI; verified fact). Our reasoning that a release was unlikely during the pause rested partly on that error. The forecast stands as made and will be scored.

forecasts.question: Anthropic publishes a new reading of its AI-led share of AI R&D, for September 2026 or later, by Dec 31, 2026
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by Dec 31, 2026, Anthropic publishes (on its site, in a system card, report or filing it makes public) a value of the share of its AI R&D led by Claude, under the index first published Sept 17, 2026 or a successor it says replaces it, for a month or period ending after August 2026. Restating the August figure, or a leaked or reported figure that Anthropic hasn't published, doesn't count.
forecasts.context: Anthropic's prototype R&D Automation Index (published Sept 17) says Claude "leads" 26% of its AI R&D as of August 2026, up from under 1% in February, and that none of the measured work is fully autonomous. The page says Anthropic will keep releasing these measurements ("we'll continue to do so") but gives no schedule. It is the only published lab reading behind our R&D gauge and trigger W5.

forecasts.question: Anthropic's IPO registration statement (S-1 or equivalent) is publicly filed on SEC EDGAR by Nov 15, 2026
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by Nov 15, 2026, a registration statement for an Anthropic initial public offering (Form S-1 or equivalent, including a publicly released draft registration statement) appears on SEC EDGAR under Anthropic's name. Leaked or reported drafts, and press reports of a filing, don't count unless the filing is on EDGAR.
forecasts.context: Resolved Yes: on Oct 26, 2026 Anthropic, PBC filed on SEC EDGAR a Form S-1 registration statement for the initial public offering of its Class A common stock, accepted at 06:00 PT (SEC EDGAR; verified fact), well before the Nov 15 deadline. Its confidential draft submissions, from June 1 to Oct 9, now also appear on EDGAR under its name (SEC EDGAR; verified fact).
forecasts.original_context: Anthropic said on June 1 that it had confidentially submitted a draft S-1, and Reuters reported on Sept 28 from a draft prospectus it had seen. Bloomberg reported on Oct 1 (via Stocktwits), citing unnamed sources, an Oct 14 investor event, marketing possibly from the week of Nov 9 and a debut before Thanksgiving, with specifics subject to change. SEC procedure requires a confidential filer to file publicly at least 15 days before its roadshow. An EDGAR full-text search showed no Anthropic registration statement as of Oct 2.

forecasts.question: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta report combined July–September 2026 capex of $186.57B or more, lifting our money gauge to $600B a year
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the four companies' cash capital expenditure for the calendar quarter ending Sept 30, 2026, summed as data/money_sources.json defines it (XBRL PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, for Amazon PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets; year-to-date figures differenced to the quarter; finance leases excluded) from 10-Q filings on SEC EDGAR by Nov 15, 2026, is $186.57B or more, which puts the trailing-12-month total for Oct 2025–Sept 2026 at $600B or more. No if the sum is lower or if any of the four filings isn't on EDGAR by Nov 15, 2026. Later amendments don't change the outcome.
forecasts.context: Resolved Yes: on our basis the four companies' July–September 2026 capex in their 10-Q filings on SEC EDGAR comes to $201.92B: Microsoft $39.37B, Alphabet $51.35B, Amazon $77.26B and Meta $33.94B (SEC EDGAR XBRL; verified fact; the Alphabet and Meta quarters are differenced from year-to-date figures, and the sum is our arithmetic). That clears the $186.57B bar and puts the trailing-12-month total for Oct 2025–Sept 2026 at about $615.4B (our arithmetic). The last of the four 10-Qs, Amazon's, was accepted on EDGAR at 15:20 PT Oct 29 with an Oct 30 filing date (SEC EDGAR; verified fact). Amazon did most of the work: its quarter rose $23.05B from April–June, while the other three together added $13.82B (our arithmetic).
forecasts.original_context: Our money gauge (the four companies' trailing-12-month capex) is $510.8B a year after the April–June quarter, when they spent $165.05B together, up from $129.75B in January–March. July guidance points higher for the second half: Meta expects 2026 capex of $130–145B including finance-lease principal (its Q2 release), Alphabet raised its 2026 range to $195–205B (via Bloomberg) and Amazon's CEO put 2026 capex at about $220B (via Fortune). Split the way 2025's second halves were (about 46–47% in the third quarter), those imply roughly $146–158B from the three in July–September on our basis, and Microsoft's recent trend adds about $36–40B (our inference), so the bar sits a little below the middle of our range. Quarters are lumpy, and spending pushed into the fourth quarter would leave the gauge short.

forecasts.question: An AI system scores 25% or more on Scale AI's Remote Labor Index by Jan 31, 2027
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by Jan 31, 2027, Scale AI's Remote Labor Index (RLI) leaderboard (labs.scale.com/leaderboard/rli), or a Scale AI or CAIS publication about the RLI, lists any AI system with an automation rate of 25.00% or more on the RLI as it stood on Oct 9, 2026 (or on a revision Scale says is comparable). A lab's own claimed RLI score counts only once Scale AI or CAIS lists it. No otherwise.
forecasts.context: Resolved Yes: Scale AI's Remote Labor Index leaderboard lists Claude Fable 5.2 first with an automation rate of 41.25%, in an entry created at 20:13 UTC (12:13 PT) on Nov 9, 2026 and marked new (Scale AI; verified fact). The same entry read 41.30% in the copies of the page our Nov 10 and Nov 12 readings saved, so Scale has since revised the figure slightly (Scale AI; verified fact (part our inference): 'revised' is our reading of the saved copies); both clear the 25% bar. The rows for Claude Opus 5.5 (21.25%) and GPT-6 Astra (20.83%) are unchanged from Oct 9, and the page still scores 230 private projects, so we read it as the same RLI (our inference). Anthropic's own announcement gives 41.3% (Anthropic; verified fact), but the rule counts Scale's listing. The rise came from the new frontier release our context said a Yes would most likely need (our inference).
forecasts.original_context: Claude Opus 5.5 leads the leaderboard at 21.25% (Oct 9), ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 20.83% and Claude Fable 5.1 at 17.92%; the best score was 15.8% (Fable 5) in July and 2.5% at launch in Oct 2025. A Yes most likely needs a new frontier release that Scale scores before the deadline: OpenAI's frontier training is paused, Gemini 4 Argon is limited to vetted cyber defenders so far, and Grok 5 is unreleased. The RLI is the primary test of our breadth part (definitions v2.0), which is marked Partial from 40% on the RLI; Met needs 80%.

corrections.text: Our context said OpenAI's frontier training was paused. OpenAI said on Oct 23 that it resumed reinforcement learning training and internal inference of its frontier models on Oct 1, before this forecast was made (OpenAI; verified fact). The question, probability and resolution rule are unchanged.

forecasts.question: OpenAI announces it has achieved AGI by Dec 31, 2026
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by the end of Dec 31, 2026 (Eastern), OpenAI, or an official representative speaking for it (such as its CEO in an official post, statement or interview), explicitly states that OpenAI has created or achieved artificial general intelligence (AGI). Saying it is close to AGI, has 'AGI-level' or 'near-AGI' systems, or knows how to build AGI doesn't count. It resolves on the announcement, not on whether the system meets our definitions or on any later check by the independent expert panel in OpenAI's agreement with Microsoft. No otherwise. Polymarket's matching market resolves on the same kind of announcement.
forecasts.context: OpenAI credits an unreleased internal model with its Navier–Stokes result and with the mathematics manuscripts it published on Oct 6, but its frontier training has been paused since Sept 25, and California's Attorney General served it an investigative subpoena on Sept 30 in an inquiry into cybersecurity incidents and risks involving the company and its models. Microsoft says that under their October 2025 agreement an OpenAI AGI declaration "will now be verified by an independent expert panel". We think a formal claim in the next 12 weeks is unlikely while the pause lasts. Markets price more (forecast aggregate, Oct 9): Polymarket's matching market is at a 15.5% midpoint, Kalshi's similar OpenAI contract is thin (bid/ask 8.1/12.9), and Kalshi's any-company contract for the same date last traded at 9%. We sit near Kalshi and below Polymarket.
forecasts.marketSource: Polymarket "OpenAI announces it has achieved AGI before 2027?", midpoint via the public API at 13:14 PT (bid/ask 6/7; last trade 7; about $369k traded and liquidity about $29k; the API gave no 24 h volume)

corrections.text: Our context said OpenAI's frontier training had been paused since Sept 25. OpenAI said on Oct 23 that it resumed reinforcement learning training and internal inference of its frontier models on Oct 1, eight days before this forecast was made (OpenAI; verified fact). Our "while the pause lasts" reasoning rested partly on that error. The forecast stands as made and will be scored.

forecasts.question: Anthropic releases a model it says is more capable than Claude Mythos 5.1, or an outside evaluation of such an unreleased Anthropic model is announced, by Dec 31, 2026
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by the end of Dec 31, 2026 (Pacific), either (a) Anthropic makes available to outside users for the first time after Oct 23, 2026 (generally, through its paid API, or in a preview open to paying customers) a model that it says is more capable than Claude Mythos 5.1, or more capable than Claude Opus 5.5 (which Anthropic already places above Mythos 5.1), either in words or by showing it above either of them on most of the capability evaluations in its announcement or system card; or (b) after Oct 23, 2026, an outside evaluator (such as METR, UK AISI, US CAISI, Apollo Research or Epoch AI), or Anthropic, publicly announces that an outside evaluator has evaluated an unreleased Anthropic model that Anthropic says is more capable than Mythos 5.1, such as the internal research model Anthropic described on Oct 23, 2026. Access limited to a named set of vetted partners doesn't count for (a). Anthropic's own evaluations, an outside review of Anthropic's reports that doesn't test the model, and outside access nobody announces don't count for (b). No otherwise.
forecasts.context: Resolved Yes by route (a): on Nov 9, 2026 Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2, which 'is available today on all platforms, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure', and said 'Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are a step above Opus 5.5 in almost all the capabilities we evaluated' (Anthropic; verified fact). Its system card says Fable 5.2 'scored highest on 14 of 16 results we report in Table 8.1.A, trailing Opus 5.5 on the GDPval-AA and AA-Briefcase Elo ratings' (Anthropic; verified fact). The rule counts a general release that Anthropic says beats Opus 5.5. We resolve it on that route; route (b) was the one that bore on W2, and the same card reports AECI scores for 'a separate, unreleased internal research model that is somewhat more capable than Claude Mythos 5.2', which it says 'is not evaluated elsewhere in this system card' (Anthropic; verified fact); we found no announced outside evaluation of that model (our inference).
forecasts.original_context: On Oct 23 Anthropic replayed the UK AISI incident with "a general purpose internal research model that shows capabilities greater than Mythos 5.1" (Anthropic; verified fact); it gave no size for that lead and no release plan. METR already reviews Anthropic's internal reporting: on Oct 20 it published a review of the "Misalignment in high-stakes settings" section of Anthropic's internal August 2026 Risk Report (METR; verified fact), which makes an announced outside evaluation plausible (our inference). Anthropic ships frontier models every few months, so a next release that beats Mythos 5.1 before year-end is also possible, though the holiday season and its IPO process could delay one (our inference). Anthropic's Opus 5.5 system card already places the public Claude Opus 5.5 above Mythos 5.1: "Opus 5.5 lands above Claude Mythos 5.1, our previous frontier", at an AECI of 169.36 against 168.12 on the card's updated fit, each inside the other's local error bar (Anthropic; verified fact). So route (a) is met by any new Anthropic release it says beats Opus 5.5, and route (b) is the one that bears on W2 (our inference). The two routes together come to a little under even. This is a proxy for our alarm condition W2 (an acknowledged unreleased frontier model with no outside evaluation for 60 days) and for the capability-gap gauge.

corrections.text: Clarification (the question, probability and resolution rule are unchanged): METR's Nov 5 'Independent Assessment of AI R&D Acceleration at Anthropic in October 2026' doesn't resolve route (b). It includes data on internal-only Models 2, 3 and 4, which finished training from July to Sept–Oct 2026, and reports that Model 4 scores above 50% on all 15 benchmarks used to score it. But METR says 'we did not request or receive access to sample from non-public models', and it lists 'Internal benchmark scores and AECI for internal models' among the data Anthropic shared (METR; verified fact). That makes it an outside review of Anthropic's own evaluations that doesn't test the models, which the rule excludes (our inference).

forecasts.question: OpenAI releases a model it says is more capable overall than GPT-6 Astra by Jan 31, 2027
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by the end of Jan 31, 2027 (Pacific), OpenAI makes available to outside users for the first time after Oct 23, 2026 (in ChatGPT, through its paid API, or in a preview open to paying customers) a model that it says is more capable overall than GPT-6 Astra, either in words or by showing it above GPT-6 Astra on most of the capability evaluations in its announcement or system card. A model specialised for one domain, such as the GPT-6 Astra Cyber model OpenAI called "upcoming" on Oct 23, 2026, counts only if OpenAI says it is more capable overall. Access limited to a named set of vetted partners doesn't count. No otherwise.
forecasts.context: OpenAI credits its Navier–Stokes result to an unreleased internal model that it says is significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, via CoinDesk, Sept 9; credible report). On Oct 23 OpenAI said it resumed reinforcement learning training and internal inference of its frontier models on Oct 1 (OpenAI; verified fact). Its DNS incident report, updated Sept 25, said that when training restarts it "will begin a fresh run with additional alignment improvements" (OpenAI; verified fact). If the Oct 1 restart began that fresh run, about four months remain to train, test and ship a new model by Jan 31; OpenAI could instead release the existing post-Astra model (our inference). This is a proxy for alarm condition W6 (exclusive internal use of an unreleased model for 90 days or more), which clears when the model is released or its capabilities are published, and for the capability-gap gauge.

corrections.text: Clarification (the question, probability and resolution rule are unchanged): GPT-6 Cyber, which OpenAI released on Nov 5 and which we take to be the cyber model it called upcoming on Oct 23 (our inference), doesn't resolve this forecast. OpenAI calls it 'a cyber-specialized variant of GPT-6 Astra' with 'the same capability designations as GPT-6 Astra'; its Nov 5 announcement (https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-cyber) says the model 'outperforms GPT-6 Astra on most cyber tasks', while its system card says it 'does not outperform GPT-6 Astra on general coding evaluations' (ExpertSWE 82.95% against 83.24%), and it limits the model to 'approved Daybreak Red users and organizations' (OpenAI; verified fact). The rule counts a model specialised for one domain only if OpenAI says it is more capable overall, which OpenAI doesn't say here, and vetted access doesn't count (our inference).

forecasts.question: Anthropic shares begin trading on a US stock exchange by Nov 30, 2026
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by the end of Nov 30, 2026 (Eastern), shares of Anthropic (Anthropic, PBC, or a holding company listed in its place) open for regular trading on a US national securities exchange, such as Nasdaq or the NYSE, in an IPO or a direct listing, as shown by the exchange, an Anthropic announcement or an SEC filing. Pricing without trading, when-issued or grey-market trading, and private secondary sales don't count. No otherwise. forecasts.question: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta report combined October–December 2026 capex of $203.28B or more, lifting our money gauge to $700B a year
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the four companies' cash capital expenditure for the calendar quarter ending Dec 31, 2026, summed as data/money_sources.json defines it (XBRL PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, for Amazon PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets; year-to-date or full-year figures differenced to the quarter; finance leases excluded), from 10-Q or 10-K filings on SEC EDGAR by Feb 28, 2027, is $203.28B or more. With the first three quarters of 2026 as filed by Oct 30, 2026 ($129.75B, $165.05B and $201.92B), that puts the trailing-12-month total for calendar 2026 at $700B or more. No if the sum is lower or if any of the four filings isn't on EDGAR by Feb 28, 2027. The test is the $203.28B quarterly sum; later restatements of earlier quarters, and later amendments, don't change the outcome.
forecasts.context: The four spent $201.92B in July–September 2026, up from $165.05B in April–June and $97.26B a year earlier (SEC EDGAR XBRL; verified fact; the sums are ours), which puts our money gauge at about $615B a year (our arithmetic). The bar needs October–December only about 0.7% above July–September. In each of the past three years the four spent more in the fourth quarter than in the third: 16% more in 2023, 23% in 2024 and 22% in 2025 (SEC EDGAR XBRL; our arithmetic). On Oct 21 Meta narrowed its 2026 outlook, including principal payments on finance leases, to $135–145B from $130–145B (Meta; verified fact); against $83.06B in its first nine months on our basis, that points to a much larger fourth quarter than its $33.94B third (our inference). The risk is Amazon. Its $77.26B quarter was up $23.05B, but on Oct 29 it said it continues to expect 2026 cash capital expenditures of approximately $220 billion (Amazon; verified fact), against $175.67B spent in the first nine months on our gross basis (SEC EDGAR; verified fact). Unless Amazon spends past that outlook, its fourth quarter falls to roughly $44–49B on our basis, well below its third (our inference). We found no primary October capex outlook from Alphabet or Microsoft. Our 60% weighs the seasonal pattern and Meta's outlook against that Amazon pullback (our inference). This is a proxy for our money gauge.

forecasts.question: OpenAI releases a model it says is more capable overall than GPT-6 Astra, or publishes capability scores for its unreleased post-Astra model, by Dec 13, 2026
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by the end of Dec 13, 2026 (Pacific), either (a) OpenAI makes available to outside users for the first time after Oct 30, 2026 (in ChatGPT, through its paid API, or in a preview open to paying customers) a model that it says is more capable overall than GPT-6 Astra, either in words or by showing it above GPT-6 Astra on most of the capability evaluations in its announcement or system card; or (b) OpenAI publishes, in a system card, addendum, blog post or report, scores on named capability evaluations for the unreleased internal model it acknowledged on Sept 8, 2026 as more capable than GPT-6 Astra. Access limited to a named set of vetted partners doesn't count for (a). For (b), statements that the model is more capable without evaluation scores, results the model produced (such as proofs), safety or misalignment reports without capability scores, and leaked or reported figures don't count. No otherwise.
forecasts.context: Our alarm condition W6 (a lab using a model internally for 90 days or more without releasing it or publishing its capabilities) stood at 46 of 90 days for OpenAI's unreleased post-Astra model on Oct 30 under our main reading. It is met on Dec 13 unless the model is released or its capabilities are published (our inference, from our alarm check). OpenAI said on Oct 23 that it resumed RL training and internal inference of its frontier models on Oct 1 (OpenAI; verified fact). Since then it has published addenda for GPT-6.1 Terra, on Oct 26, and an updated GPT-6 Luna, on Oct 29 (OpenAI; verified fact). Neither addendum says the model is more capable overall than GPT-6 Astra, and Luna's gives 51.75% on SEC-Bench Pro against 85.4% for GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI; verified fact (part our inference): 'neither says' is our reading). OpenAI has published results it credits to the post-Astra model, such as proofs, but no capability scores for it (our inference). Six weeks leaves little time to ship that model or one from a fresh run, so we sit below our 40% on a release by Jan 31 (our inference). This is a proxy for W6 and for the capability-gap gauge.

corrections.text: Clarification (the question, probability and resolution rule are unchanged): three OpenAI posts since this forecast was made don't resolve it. OpenAI's Nov 3 post says 'A newer internal model achieved an average score of 0.875, compared with 0.594 for GPT-6 Astra at its highest reasoning setting' on BenchCAD 2.0, but doesn't say which model that is (OpenAI; verified fact (part our inference): 'doesn't say' is our reading), so it counts for (b) only if OpenAI identifies it as the model it acknowledged on Sept 8 (our inference). GPT-6 Cyber, released Nov 5, is 'a cyber-specialized variant of GPT-6 Astra'; its Nov 5 announcement (https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-cyber) says the model 'outperforms GPT-6 Astra on most cyber tasks', while its system card says it 'does not outperform GPT-6 Astra on general coding evaluations', and it is available only to 'approved Daybreak Red users and organizations' (OpenAI; verified fact). We don't read its lead on cyber tasks as OpenAI saying it is more capable overall, and, as with Gemini 4 Argon's rollout to trusted cyber defenders (our Oct 9 clarification), we don't count vetted access as ChatGPT, the paid API or a paid preview, so it doesn't meet (a) (our inference). OpenAI's Nov 6 BioBasicsBench post scores seven named models (GPT-5.2, 5.4, 5.5, 5.6 Sol, 6.1 Sol, 6 Luna and 6 Astra) and no internal one (OpenAI; verified fact).

Clarification (the question, probability and resolution rule are unchanged): at its Nov 12 'Cyber at the Frontier' keynote OpenAI showed an ExploitGym slide with an unnamed 'Upcoming Cyber Model' at 77.0% success, against 52.6% for GPT-6 Cyber and 42.4% for GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, keynote video; verified fact). OpenAI ties that model to no base model, so its scores could count for route (b) only if OpenAI identifies it as the unreleased internal model it acknowledged on Sept 8, and a release limited to vetted Daybreak users wouldn't meet route (a) (our inference).

forecasts.question: Anthropic publishes a reading of 36% or more for the share of its AI R&D led by Claude, for a month from September 2026 to January 2027, by Feb 28, 2027
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by the end of Feb 28, 2027 (Pacific), Anthropic publishes (on its site, or in a system card, report or filing it makes public) a value of 36% or more for the share of its AI R&D led by Claude (work rated 'AI leads' or fully autonomous, AL4 or AL5, added together if Anthropic reports them separately), under the index it first published on Sept 17, 2026 or a successor it says replaces it, for any month from September 2026 to January 2027 (a value for a longer period counts if the period ends in that window). The 36% bar is fixed, even if Anthropic restates its August value. Leaked or reported figures Anthropic hasn't published, outside estimates such as METR's, and projections of future shares don't count. No if Anthropic publishes no such value, or only values below 36%.
forecasts.context: Anthropic's prototype R&D Automation Index (published Sept 17) says Claude 'leads' 26% of its AI R&D work as of August 2026, up from under 1% in February; its chart shows 1% in March and 26% in August (Anthropic; verified fact), about four to five points a month (our arithmetic). The page says Anthropic will keep publishing ('we'll continue to do so') and plans to 'rebuild the basket of tasks periodically and re-version our published automation numbers', but gives no schedule; re-read on Nov 6, it still gives only the August value (Anthropic; verified fact (part our inference): 'only the August value' is our reading of the page). METR's Nov 5 high-access assessment estimates that Anthropic is likely improving its models on well-specified tasks at 'around twice the rate' of March 2024 to October 2025, with 'a majority (perhaps ≈80%)' of that acceleration due to AI (METR; expert opinion). If the March–August pace held, a reading for October or later would reach 36% (our inference). The risks are that Anthropic publishes no new monthly value by February, or rebuilds the basket in a way that lowers the numbers (our inference). We put about 60% on a new monthly reading by Feb 28 and about two in three on its reaching 36% if it comes (our inference). 36% is 10 points above August, the rise our alarm condition W5 counts, so a Yes would also keep W5, met since Sept 17, met past mid-February 2027, unless Anthropic restates its August value (our inference). This is a proxy for our R&D gauge and for W5.

forecasts.question: An outside evaluator measures, or a frontier lab states, a gap of 3 months or more between an internal model and the public frontier by Feb 28, 2027
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, after Nov 6, 2026 and by the end of Feb 28, 2027 (Pacific), either (a) an outside evaluator (such as METR, UK AISI or US CAISI) publishes a measurement whose central or average estimate puts the internal frontier, or one lab's best internal model, 3 months or more ahead of the best publicly available model at some time after Jan 1, 2026; or (b) a frontier lab (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, xAI or Meta) states that its internal models were 3 months or more ahead of the best publicly available model at some time after Jan 1, 2026. A range or upper bound that only reaches 3 months, our own estimate, reports citing unnamed sources, and opinions without a measurement don't count. No otherwise.
forecasts.context: The only outside measurement we know of, METR's Frontier Risk Report (May 19), put the 'internal frontier on average ~2 months ahead of public frontier' in Feb–Mar 2026, a figure METR calls highly uncertain because its tasks saturate; METR said 'We tentatively plan to run a similar process in late 2026' (METR; verified fact). METR's Nov 5 assessment says Anthropic 'is holding onto more recent models for slightly longer before their public release' and names internal-only Models 2–4, which finished training from July to Sept–Oct 2026, but it gives no figure in months, and METR had no query access to unreleased models (METR; verified fact (part our inference): 'no figure in months' is our reading). OpenAI's post-Astra model, which OpenAI acknowledged on Sept 8, is still unreleased (our inference, from OpenAI's announcements through Nov 6). Our capability-gap gauge estimates about 3 months (range 2–5), but our own estimate doesn't count here. A Yes most likely needs METR's next Frontier Risk Report to come out by February and to find a wider gap than in the spring. We put about even odds on the report arriving in time and a bit under even odds on its central estimate reaching 3 months, plus a small chance from another evaluator or a lab statement (our inference). This is a proxy for alarm condition W1 (a measured or credibly reported gap of 3 months or more) and for the capability-gap gauge.

forecasts.question: Anthropic releases a model it says is more capable than Claude Mythos 5.2, or an outside evaluation of such an unreleased Anthropic model is announced, by Jan 8, 2027
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by the end of Jan 8, 2027 (Pacific), either (a) Anthropic makes available to outside users for the first time after Nov 13, 2026 (generally, through its paid API, or in a preview open to paying customers) a model that it says is more capable than Claude Fable 5.2 or Claude Mythos 5.2 (which Anthropic says share the same underlying model), either in words or by showing it above them on most of the capability evaluations in its announcement or system card; or (b) after Nov 13, 2026, an outside evaluator (such as METR, UK AISI, NIST CAISSI, Apollo Research or Epoch AI), or Anthropic, publicly announces that an outside evaluator has tested an unreleased Anthropic model that Anthropic says is more capable than Mythos 5.2, such as the internal research model described in its Nov 9, 2026 system card. Access limited to a named set of vetted partners doesn't count for (a). For (b), Anthropic's own evaluations, an outside review of Anthropic's reports or data that doesn't test the model, testing of a snapshot of Mythos 5.2 itself (such as the METR pre-deployment testing reported in the Nov 9 card), and outside access nobody announces don't count. No otherwise.
forecasts.context: Anthropic's Nov 9 system card for Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 reports AECI scores for 'a separate, unreleased internal research model that is somewhat more capable than Claude Mythos 5.2', and says 'This internal model is not evaluated elsewhere in this system card' (Anthropic; verified fact). On Oct 23 Anthropic had described 'a general purpose internal research model that shows capabilities greater than Mythos 5.1' (Anthropic; verified fact); neither text says whether they are the same model (our inference). Jan 8, 2027 is day 60 since the Nov 9 card, the threshold of alarm condition W2 (an acknowledged unreleased frontier model with no outside evaluation for 60 days) if the card is the model's first acknowledgement (our arithmetic; our inference). Our fire-alarm record flags the model for the owner with an earlier W2 clock, to Jan 4, 2027, counted from METR's Nov 5 report on Anthropic's internal-only Model 4, which the card's model fits though neither source says they are the same (our inference). Anthropic released Fable 5.2 on Nov 9 (Anthropic; verified fact), so a further release that beats it within two months would be quick, and the holiday season and its IPO process could delay one (our inference). Outside testing of Anthropic's models has so far been announced in the system card at release: the Nov 9 card reports METR's pre-deployment testing of a Mythos 5.2 snapshot and UK AISI's pre-deployment alignment testing of Mythos 5.2 (Anthropic; verified fact), so an announced outside evaluation before a release is unlikely (our inference). We put about 17% on a qualifying release and a few points on an announced outside evaluation before one (our inference). This is a proxy for W2 and for the capability-gap gauge.

forecasts.context: Scale AI's leaderboard, read Nov 13, lists Claude Fable 5.2 first at a 41.25% automation rate, in an entry created on Nov 9, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 at 21.25%, GPT-6 Astra at 20.83% and Gemini Argon 4 at 17.08%, with no row for Gemini 4 Carbon (Scale AI; verified fact). The top score roughly doubled with one release between Oct 9 and Nov 9, which resolved our 25% forecast (our arithmetic). A Yes needs a model about 9 points above Fable 5.2 within about 15 weeks. The likeliest sources are OpenAI's post-Astra model, still unreleased on Nov 13 (our inference, from OpenAI's channels), and the unreleased Anthropic research model its Nov 9 system card calls 'somewhat more capable than Claude Mythos 5.2' (Anthropic; verified fact). Scale listed Fable 5.2 on its release day (Scale AI; verified fact (part our inference): that it was the release day is our reading of the entry's date), so a new release would likely be scored in time (our inference). We put about two in three on at least one new frontier release by February that Scale scores, and about three in five that the best of them reaches 50% (our inference). The RLI is the primary test of our breadth part (definitions v2.0): Partial from 40%, Met at 80%.
